cause.label: no_identifiable_cause
cause.what_happened: Host Digital (ex-Healthy Choice Wellness, renamed and relisted as HOST on NYSE American on 2026-09-18 after a merger with Host Digital Infrastructure LLC, then a $17.5m Cantor-led offering at $8.00) fell a further 7.2% by 15:04 ET on 1.57x volume, almost all intraday, with no filing or wire story found dated today; it is the sixth >5% fall since listing and leaves the stock at $3.60, 55% below the offering price.

evidence.claim: Underwritten offering of 2,187,500 Class A shares at $8.00, closing 2026-09-21, Cantor representative
Last 8-K before the drop is a CEO shareholder letter (Item 7.01) of 2026-09-29, Site I delivery targeted Q1 2027, no price or financing news
Merger closing 8-K carries going-concern language (substantial doubt)
Filing list shows no filing dated 2026-10-01 or 2026-10-02

pipeline.next_dated_event: first lock-up early-release tranche (day 30 of the 180-day lock-up) and the registration-rights resale shelf deadline (30 days after 2026-09-17 closing), both about 2026-10-17, outside the window
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: a resale S-1/S-3 from the merger holders filed before the deadline, or an 8-K on Site I tenant/financing, landing on 2026-10-05.

positioning_check: Short interest unavailable in the baseline (Nasdaq returned no settlements for this freshly relisted NYSE American name); no option chain, so no skew. Float: 28.2m Class A outstanding after the offering plus 19.9m pre-funded warrants (48.2m fully diluted), per the 2026-09-17 prospectus supplement; most non-offering shares sit under a 180-day lock-up. Nasdaq insider summary shows one open-market buy in 3 months, undated in the feed.

findings.finding: The issuer agreed a 45-day company lock-up from the 2026-09-17 prospectus supplement, so no ATM draw, follow-on or primary sale can price tonight or on 2026-10-05 without the underwriter's consent; the commonest second leg for a fallen small cap is structurally absent from this window.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The lock-up runs to about 2026-11-01, covering the whole window; the absence of an issuance is what the window will show.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every post-listing fall (9-17, 9-18, 9-25, 9-28, 10-01) was followed by a lower next close in the baseline despite no new issuance after 9-21, so the absence of supply has not stopped the decline so far.
findings.why_not_priced: The tape treats a micro-cap with going-concern language as an ATM candidate; the price would carry no issuance discount at all if readers knew the company is barred, but this is a weak, partly known fact and the 9-17 ATM-language hit in the forward block keeps that fear alive.
findings.independence: The 8-K of 2026-09-21 describes only the Cantor underwriting with no ATM (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948864/000149315226043572/form8-k.htm); the 2026-09-17 ex10-1 'at-the-market' hit is a registration rights agreement, not an ATM (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1948864/000149315226043135/ex10-1.htm).

outside_window.finding: First early-release tranche of the 180-day insider lock-up (one fifth of lock-up securities at day 30, roughly 2026-10-17) adds supply from merger holders

Registration Rights Agreement requires a resale shelf filed within 30 days of the 2026-09-17 merger closing; filing is permitted under the lock-up and would put a resale prospectus over 19.9m pre-funded warrant shares and merger units
Site I (43 MW, $1.25bn base rent take-or-pay) targets delivery Q1 2027; rent starts on delivery
